name: The Vesper Gate

detectability.signature: Paired gamma flares at each aperture with gravimetric shear ripples radiating on every pulse cycle

proximity: Compass headings rotate slowly toward the throat regardless of intended course
Sensor returns lag by several seconds within 500 km of either aperture
contact: Transit hurls vessels eleven light-years to the terminus in seconds
Hull plating hums audibly as spacetime shear grips the frame during passage
prolonged_exposure: Loitering inside the throat risks exit displacement of thousands of kilometers
Survey crews stationed nearby report chronic instrument recalibration failures

known_incidents: The corvette Halcyon Step exited sixty thousand kilometers off-target after transiting off-phase
Builder-era anchor rings still hold both apertures open against gravitational collapse
description: The Vesper Gate hangs in dark space as a ring of weathered builder alloy nine kilometers across, its aperture filled with a slow swirl of lensed starlight from somewhere else. Sensor sweeps return paired gamma signatures, one at each mouth, and a faint shear ripple that washes outward every ninety-one minutes. No natural process explains the anchor structures fused to the ring's rim.

The corridor pulses. During an open phase, transit is swift and comparatively gentle, spitting ships out at the far terminus seconds later. Between pulses the throat narrows and transits become a gamble, sometimes depositing vessels thousands of kilometers from their intended exit vector. Navigators time their runs against the pulse clock and pray the schedule holds.

Discovered by a survey frigate that stumbled through while fleeing pirates, the Gate opened an eleven-light-year shortcut that reshaped regional trade almost overnight. Whoever built it vanished from history, leaving only the rings and a geometry no modern engineer can replicate. The Halcyon Step incident taught the fleet to treat off-phase transits as emergencies rather than inconveniences.

Both apertures are now garrisoned, and toll schedules publish the pulse timing to licensed traffic. Smugglers gamble on gap windows between pulses; researchers drift at a respectful distance trying to reverse-engineer the anchors. For now the Gate holds, but every pulse is a reminder that eight-century-old machinery owes nothing to its users.
